newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schaeuble - Bonn weighs delaying debt repayment.
newsitem.headline: Schaeuble - Bonn weighs delaying debt repayment.

text.p: Wolfgang Schaeuble, parliamentary leader of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats, said on Wednesday the coalition was weighing delaying repayments on east German and railway debt in the coming year to help solve its budget crisis.

Current budget negotiations within the coalition have considered the delays on payments for the German Unity Fund and old debt from the national railway, but have not reached any conclusions, Schaeuble told journalists.
Finance Minister Theo Waigel has said in the past ad hoc measures such as privatisations or delayed debt repayments would make economic sense to stabilise the fiscal healing process.
Waigel's budget for 1998 is due to be submitted to the cabinet next week.
Germany, like other European nations, is struggling to rein in its budget deficit this year to qualify for economic and monetary union (EMU), due to start in 1999.
